paragraphs: Plymouth City Council's own fostering service is called Foster for Plymouth, a not-for-profit service run by the council. Children in care in the city live with its carers or with independent agencies, including those listed on this page.

In May 2025 the council said 534 children were in its care, while Foster for Plymouth had 119 fostering households and 32 kinship carers. When there are not enough local homes, children can end up in residential care or with foster families outside the city, away from their friends, family and school, which is why the council is asking for more local carers.

Foster for Plymouth recruits for time-limited and permanent fostering, emergency care of up to two weeks, respite, parent and child placements, and Step Forward, a scheme for children with higher needs who are moving on from residential care. The council said in 2025 that carers receive between £350 and £779 per child each week, made up of an allowance and a reward payment, depending on the child's age and needs, with more for Step Forward. There are extra payments for birthdays, holidays, festivals and proms, and many carers get a 50 per cent council tax discount or full exemption, including some living outside the city.

Carers have a supervising social worker, training, peer support and social events, and since December 2024 the service has run the Mockingbird programme, where a hub carer supports a small group of nearby fostering families. You need to be over 21 with a spare bedroom. Talk to Foster for Plymouth and to two or three of the agencies below before you choose.
